severity: CRITICAL -- v1 and v2 both award success to a pipette thrown into the air
source: External review of the reward and RL setup.

1_reach_grasp_xy_only.claim: Reach/grasp used only x,y; z and contact ignored.
1_reach_grasp_xy_only.verified: CONFIRMED in code: v1/v2 computed fingertip-barrel distance as norm((fing-barrel)[:, :2]) -- the xy projection. A hand hovering 20 cm above the pipette scored a perfect reach, and grasp required only that fingers and thumb be near the AXIS, not near the object and not on opposite sides of it.
1_reach_grasp_xy_only.fix: v3 uses full 3-D distance, adds a height gate (GRASP_DZ=0.075) and an OPPOSITION test (thumb and finger-group offset vectors must have negative dot product, and span < GRASP_SPAN). The scene ships NO contact sensors (verified by enumerating every scene entity), so v3 does not claim to read contact forces; it uses the strongest measured geometric proxy and labels it as such via info['grasp_is_geometric_proxy'].

2_lift_by_throwing.claim: 'lift' only tested height, so throwing the pipette upward satisfied it.
2_lift_by_throwing.verified: CONFIRMED for v1. v2 added a negative ballistic-speed test.
2_lift_by_throwing.fix: v3 makes the condition positive: lift fires only when the pipette is GRASPED (3-D, opposing) AND above LIFT_H AND slow. A thrown object fails the grasp conjunct the moment it leaves the hand.

3_success_in_the_sky.claim: Success is reached when the pipette is thrown upward and velocity=0 in the sky.
3_success_in_the_sky.verified: CONFIRMED AND REPRODUCED. v1/v2 tested 'over the pot in xy, above PLATE_Z=0.95, and |dz| < 2e-3 between consecutive steps'. At a throw's apex vertical velocity passes through zero, satisfying 'settled' in mid-air. Direct demonstration: a pipette placed at z=1.60 (about 0.8 m above the pot), released, motionless, scores success=True under BOTH the v1 and v2 predicates.
3_success_in_the_sky.fix: v3 requires the pipette to be at rest AND supported AND released: speed below REST_SPEED for REST_STEPS=10 CONSECUTIVE steps (a single zero-crossing cannot satisfy a window), height inside a resting BAND relative to the pot (PLATE_REST_DZ=(0.05,0.22), so mid-air fails), and not currently grasped.

4_no_smoothness_term.claim: You may need a smoothing term to punish high-frequency motion.
4_no_smoothness_term.verified: CONFIRMED: no reward-side smoothness term existed in v1 or v2.
4_no_smoothness_term.fix: v3 adds a bounded penalty on the OBJECT's jerk while held (W_JERK, capped at JERK_PENALTY_CAP per step so it can never dominate task reward, and applied only while held so free-space motion is untaxed). This complements the training-time CAPS action penalty (SMOOTH_LAMBDA), which is validated separately in g1_piston_rl_induced_oscillation.json.

5_stale_reward_validation.claim: Reward validation seems to be outdated.
5_stale_reward_validation.verified: CONFIRMED: the only reward validation on record lives in g1_piston_demo_screen_manifest.json and was computed under the v1 transport-only predicate, before the plunger DoF was discovered.
5_stale_reward_validation.fix: tools/g1_piston/validate_reward.py re-derives validation per reward version.

status: v3 implemented; 18 tests pin every fix, including a test that reproduces the sky-throw exploit and asserts v3 rejects it.

self_audit_findings.method: Adversarial probing of v3 itself after implementing the review fixes.

exploit_found_and_fixed.name: press-after-release farming
exploit_found_and_fixed.mechanism: `grasp` is a LATCHED stage. Gating the plunger shaping term and the press/dispense stages on the latched stage let a policy grasp once, release the pipette, and then drive the plunger down by any other means -- e.g. pressing it against the table -- while the term kept paying.
exploit_found_and_fixed.measured: 18.00 reward farmed across four presses after releasing.
exploit_found_and_fixed.fix: Gate the plunger shaping term and the press/dispense stages on the LIVE `grasped` predicate instead of the latched stage. Post-fix the same sequence pays -0.004.

probes_that_passed.approach_oscillation: 30 approach/retreat cycles: cycle 1 pays 3.958 (one-time approach shaping plus reach and grasp bonuses), cycles 2-30 pay -0.002 each, i.e. only the step cost. Best-so-far shaping holds.
probes_that_passed.transport_oscillation: 20 toward/away-from-pot cycles while held: total -2.200 (net negative).
probes_that_passed.reach_without_opposition: Fingers and thumb on the same side at 0.044 m: reach and grasp both refused.
probes_that_passed.jerk_avoidance: Releasing avoids the jerk penalty (0.100 -> 0.000) but forfeits lift, press and success, so it is not a profitable deviation.

wiring_defects_found_and_fixed.v3_not_in_eval_or_render: REWARD_V3 was wired into train_sac.py only, so a v3-trained policy could not be scored or filmed under v3 -- evaluation would have silently fallen back to the exploitable v1/v2 predicate. Now wired into eval_checkpoint.py and render_rollouts.py.
wiring_defects_found_and_fixed.demo_buffer_guard_v2_only: The guard hard-coded reward_version == 'v2_functional', so a matched v3 run was wrongly refused while a v3 buffer under v1 training passed silently. Now compares built-vs-trained for every version.

self_audit_findings.execution_verification: Verified by running, not by reading: all three rewards load and step through the tools' own import path; the critic accepts all four ACTION_BASIS/CRITIC_STATE combinations with correct widths; actor gradients reach all 30 horizon steps through the DCT basis; CriticStateBuilder resolves every hardcoded joint and body name against the real scene enumeration and produces the expected slot values.

grasp_predicate_calibration.why: The first v3 grasp test (3-D distance to the barrel CENTRE plus opposition of thumb and fingers about that centre) was designed from intuition. Before trusting it, it was measured against a real 690-step RLPD@415k rollout on the frozen condition.
grasp_predicate_calibration.finding: Both original conditions were wrong for this object. (1) The barrel is a 0.19 m CYLINDER, so gripping it anywhere along its length puts the hand up to ~0.095 m from its centre -- a 0.045 m distance-to-centre threshold was unsatisfiable by construction, and the predicate scored 0 of 690 steps. (2) The Inspire hand grips a cylinder by curling the four fingers around it with the thumb bracing from the SAME side: the opposition cosine never went negative and the thumb sits closer to the axis than the fingers. 'Thumb opposite the fingers' describes a pinch, which is not this grasp.
grasp_predicate_calibration.recalibration: Grasp now tests RADIAL distance to the barrel AXIS (the right measure for a cylinder) plus whether the contact height lies WITHIN the barrel's extent (|dz| < BARREL_HALF_H = 0.095), plus a closed-hand span. Opposition is retained in the info dict as a descriptive statistic but is no longer a gate.
grasp_predicate_calibration.validation: On the same measured rollout the recalibrated predicate fires on 22 of 690 steps, and it rejects all 169 steps where the hand is near the axis but ABOVE the barrel's extent -- every one of which v1/v2 counted as a grasp. So the reviewer's original point stands and is now enforced correctly: the xy-only test was crediting hovers.
grasp_predicate_calibration.regression_guard: test_the_measured_geometry_satisfies_the_calibrated_predicate replays the real measured geometry through the predicate and fails if it ever becomes unsatisfiable again, or if it starts accepting the off-object hover case.

implication_for_reported_grasp_rate: The v1/v2 grasp_rate of ~1.00 reported throughout this study counts steps where the hand is near the barrel AXIS regardless of height. On the measured rollout 169 of the 191 qualifying steps (88%) have the hand OFF the object in z. The headline 'RL learned to grasp' claim should therefore be restated as 'RL learned to bring the hand to the barrel axis', pending re-scoring under the v3 predicate.
